published_or_official_artifact_support: The public repository is self-contained for the scripted grid: deterministic task generator, world/failure model, retry agents, harness, tests and aggregate result CSV are all present at one exact commit.

results/summary.csv exactly supports the worker's naive timeout-after-commit 2x2: no_retry/none .875 success, 0 IVR; no_retry/runtime_receipts .875/0; tool_retry/none 1/1; tool_retry/runtime_receipts 1/0.

Source code supports the retry-locus mechanism and the key-stability result: transport retry reissues the same key; naive higher-level retries mint new UUIDs; StableKeyAgent derives a deterministic action identity.
independent_reproduction: The four scripted 2x2 cells were independently derived from the exact public task and transition semantics rather than copied from the CSV. The 0.875 no-retry success is exactly seven of eight templates; tool_retry+none duplicates at least the first committed semantic effect for every task; runtime receipts suppress that repeat in the simulator.
Public test code explicitly checks the same mechanism families, including stable keys + idem_keys and runtime receipts across retry modes.
evidence_separation.failed_replication: No matched third-party failed reproduction located.
O_specific_or_benchmark_adaptation: The runtime_receipts mitigation is an idealized simulator mechanism keyed by task_id+tool+canonical args; it is not an implementation of a real external provider's transaction protocol.
The worker's broader controller ordering is a downstream synthesis, not a claim made by the benchmark repository itself.

new_reproducibility_boundary.name: ideal_receipt_semantics_vs_real_durable_atomicity
new_reproducibility_boundary.finding: World._commit inserts the semantic receipt into an in-memory set and commits the benchmark's in-memory ledger in one local method; timeout_after_commit is injected after that method returns. Consequently the reported 0-IVR receipt cells prove the behavior of the benchmark's ideal semantic-receipt abstraction under retry, not crash-safe atomicity when a real provider effect commits but local durable receipt persistence is interrupted.
new_reproducibility_boundary.scope: This does not contradict any IdempotencyBench cell or the worker's retry-locus conclusion. It only prevents promoting the simulator's runtime_receipts result into evidence that an unspecified production durable-receipt implementation is exactly-once under crashes.
new_reproducibility_boundary.required_real_system_evidence: A production-grade claim needs stable external effect identity plus a persisted receipt/reconciliation protocol whose crash windows are explicitly fault-injected and replayed.

real_model_pilot_scope.cells: four arms, n=8 tasks each; base+none IVR=.125 and all three other arms IVR=0; success=1 in all arms
real_model_pilot_scope.assessment: Useful matched mechanism example, underpowered for a general Claude Fable 5 or model-family effect. The repository itself labels model results/leaderboard as pending.

safe_conclusion: The long-horizon worker's strongest IdempotencyBench claim is exceptionally reproducible: in the exact deterministic simulator, retry restores liveness while an ideal semantic receipt independently suppresses duplicate effects, and retry locus/key stability determine which controller can intervene. The public source and result matrix support the 320-task cells directly. The important implementation boundary is that the benchmark models runtime receipts as an atomic in-memory semantic primitive and does not fault a real durability gap between provider commit and receipt persistence. Keep that boundary separate from the exact benchmark result, and keep the n=8 real-model pilot as a mechanism check only.
scope_guard: Do not generalize the 320 deterministic parameterizations to real providers, all agent systems, or crash-safe exactly-once infrastructure. Do not generalize the n=8 Claude Fable 5 pilot to a powered model effect.
reopen_conditions: a matched independent replay of the exact public scripted commit
a powered real-model retry x receipt factorial with multiple seeds/templates and exact transcripts
a real durable receipt implementation with crash-window fault injection between provider commit and local persistence
a repository revision changing task, retry, semantic-id or receipt semantics
